The implementation of the ReactMemoryProfiler utility and the
withMemoryProfiling HOC looks like a great start for addressing Issue
#36722. Using FinalizationRegistry for tracking unmounted components is a
solid approach for modern environments.

Regarding the 35-50% memory reduction and 95%+ leak detection accuracy
mentioned earlier in the thread, could you clarify how those figures were
obtained? It would be helpful to know if those were based on internal
benchmarks or preliminary testing with these utilities.


On Sun, Jun 21, 2026, 1:03 PM Vaibhav0377 ***@***.***> wrote:

> *Vaibhav0377* left a comment (react/react#36722)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36722#issuecomment-4762832140>
>
> // withMemoryProfiling.js
> import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
> import { memoryProfiler } from './ReactMemoryProfiler';
>
> export function withMemoryProfiling(WrappedComponent) {
> return function ProfiledComponent(props) {
> const componentIdRef = useRef(null);
> const componentName = WrappedComponent.displayName ||
> WrappedComponent.name || 'Component';
>
> if (!componentIdRef.current) {
>   componentIdRef.current = memoryProfiler.trackMount(componentName, this);
> }
>
> useEffect(() => {
>   // Start global monitoring on first component mount
>   memoryProfiler.start();
>
>   return () => {
>     memoryProfiler.trackUnmount(componentIdRef.current, componentName);
>   };
> }, []);
>
> return <WrappedComponent {...props} />;
>
> };
> } Step 2: Higher-Order Component (HOC) / Hook for Integration
> To inject this into 50+ React applications easily without modifying
> internal logic, developers can wrap suspect components or use a global
> useEffect scanner.
